.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures continue 
through at least Tuesday with much needed rain chances mid to late 
week.

Broad 1032-1035 mb high pressure will remain anchored northeast of 
the area today while continuing it's influence across the Mid-
Atlantic region. The high pressure will shift off the southern 
NJ/Delmarva coast Monday before meandering back overhead Tuesday. At 
the surface, expect a continuation of seasonable temperatures and 
dry conditions. High temperatures will push into the 60s for most 
with overnight lows in the upper 30s and low 40s.

Sunshine will be filtered at times today and Monday as a weak 
shortwave trough slides south of the region. Expect a thin broken to 
overcast deck of high level cirrus this morning giving way to breaks 
of filtered sunshine this afternoon. High level clouds return with 
onshore flow Monday before dissipating Tuesday as high pressure 
settles back over the region. Winds will remain light while turning 
to the south today before shifting to the east and southeast Monday 
into Tuesday. This will allow highs Tuesday to get back into the low 
70s

Wednesday will be the day of transition as a deepening upper level 
trough pivots east from the Upper Midwest and Great Plains region. 
At the surface, will be an area of low pressure ejecting out of the 
mid-Mississippi River Valley/Mid-South ejecting north and east 
toward the central Appalachians and Carolina/VA coast Thursday into 
Friday. This will be our first widespread rain across the region in 
more than 2 weeks. Current 00z guidance suggest any widespread rain 
holding off until late Wednesday night and carrying through most of 
the day Thursday as low pressure passes over the region. A much 
needed soaking rainfall is expect with the probabilities of 1" of 
rain around 15-25 percent. Most guidance suggest rainfall amounts of 
0.50-1" of rain over the Thursday through Friday timeframe. Of 
course this is subject to change based upon the track of the low 
pressure system late week. Surface high pressure builds overhead in 
the wake of the low pressure system, with diminishing rain chances 
expected heading into the upcoming weekend.  High temperatures will 
be in the upper 60s to low 70s east of the Blue Ridge with those 
along and west in the upper 50s to 60s. Overnight low temperatures 
will be in the 50s each night. Lows drop into the 40s east of the 
Blue Ridge Thursday and Friday night.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
No significant impacts are expected to aviators through at least 
Tuesday. VFR conditions will prevail along with dry conditions. 
Expect broken to overcast high level cirrus this morning giving way 
to scattered to broken high clouds this afternoon. Broken to 
overcast high level cirrus returns tonight into Monday with light 
onshore flow. Winds will turn to the south today before shifting to 
the east and southeast Monday at less than 15 kts. Some patchy fog 
is possible in the river valleys Monday and Tuesday morning given a 
slight uptick in moisture from weakened onshore flow and ahead of 
the incumbent trough mid to late week.

Wednesday will be the day of transition across the region. Expect 
increasing mid and high level clouds, especially during the 
afternoon and evening hours. VFR conditions will prevail until 
Wednesday evening with any precipitation holding off until Wednesday 
night or Thursday morning. Widespread sub-VFR conditions are 
increasingly likely Thursday and Friday as low pressure works across 
the region. Periods of rain are expected both days leading to 
lowering cigs and vsbys. Winds will remain out of the south and 
southeast at less than 15 kts through Thursday.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through at least Tuesday. Winds will 
remain light out of the east and southeast today through Monday as 
high pressure pushes offshore. The high will settle back over the 
region Tuesday before centering itself over the western Atlantic mid 
to late week. This will lead to southerly winds and potential SCA 
channeling mainly over the open waters late Tuesday into Wednesday. 

Low pressure will pass west of the waters Thursday with a secondary 
wave of low pressure passing to the east Friday. Winds will remain 
near or just below SCA levels both days with widespread rain 
expected. High pressure returns into the upcoming weekend.
